name: Watercolor Storybook
summary: Transparent watercolour washes and loose, broken ink lines on warm cold-pressed paper: a living illustrated fairy-tale book.
description: The whole game looks like a page from an illustrated children's book. The ground is a per-pixel pigment simulation over cream paper (absorbance mixing, darker pooled wash edges, bare paper gaps, granulation, pale dapples), dotted with inked grass tufts and tiny flowers. Characters are layered washes with wet-in-wet colour blooms and a misregistered, variable-width sepia ink contour that is deliberately broken in 2-3 places. A deckled bare-paper margin frames the screen like a book page.
bestFor: top-down survivor / action games with a fairy-tale theme
avoidFor: games that need hundreds of unique animated sprites generated at runtime

difficulty.why: A painterly quality for every new asset takes many iterations; performance was already tight and the style takes 1-3 s to load (bake).

technique.resolution: Native resolution, smooth scaling. Sprites baked at 3 px per world unit (gems 4, small FX 4-6); ground chunks rendered per pixel at up to 2.5 px per world unit (256-unit chunks).
technique.summary: Every colour is laid down as a transparent wash: either per pixel in absorbance space (paper * exp(-absorbance)) for the ground, or on a scratch canvas (fill + blurred blobs + rim + grain multiply, clipped) for sprites, then overlaid with tapered sepia ink lines that are offset from the wash by ~0.45/0.35 units.
technique.linework: Sepia ink #2a1b14 (blue-black #252c46 for ghosts and forest grass). Lines are filled ribbons, not strokes: width 0.7-0.95 units for body contours, 1.5 for a brute, 0.3-0.45 for details; tapered at both ends (first 12-30 %, last 16-40 %), pressure wobble 0.6*sin(s*0.8)+0.4*sin(s*2.1) at 30 %, thicker on the side away from the upper-left light (light factor 0.45-0.6). Contours are broken into 2-3 pieces with small overshoots. Round caps and joins.
technique.shading: Wet-in-wet: blurred ellipses of lighter (top-left) and darker (bottom-right) pigment inside each shape (blur 0.5-2.6 units, alpha 0.4-0.95), a radial paper-white highlight at 30 %/26 % of the bbox, and a blurred darker rim stroke (1-1.8 units, alpha 0.5-0.65) imitating pigment pooling at the wash edge. Hatching only on the shadow side of big rocks and brutes.
technique.lighting: Light from the upper left (direction -0.6, -0.8). Shadows are one shared indigo glaze rgba(50,54,92,0.2) per frame (union Path2D), lighter 0.11 for floating enemies. Carved faces, cracks and lanterns glow with warm yellow washes plus an additive radial glow sprite (alpha ~0.3, flickering).
technique.texture: Cold-pressed paper tooth, pigment granulation (multiplied grain canvas), wash-flow noise for edges and dapples, pale backrun bloom rings and pigment splatter baked into the ground; deckled bare-paper page margin on screen.

paletteRules: The paper is always the lightest value; never use pure white #ffffff except tiny specular dots (rgba 255,253,244).
Ground stays mid-light and low-chroma (meadow ~55 %, path ~10 %, fields/forest the rest) so the saturated characters (pumpkin orange, violet, indigo) pop.
Mix ground colours in absorbance space (subtractive), not by alpha-blending RGB: overlapping washes get darker and richer, never greyer.
Every shape has a lighter top-left and darker bottom-right pigment blob of a neighbouring hue (orange -> yellow-ochre / burnt sienna, violet -> lilac / plum).
Ink is warm sepia #2a1b14, never pure black; cold subjects (ghosts, forest) switch to blue-black #252c46.
Shadows are indigo glazes (50,54,92), never black or grey.

background.summary: A per-pixel watercolour shader paints biome washes (meadow, forest, golden field, dirt path) over paper in absorbance space, with pooled dark edges, bare-paper gaps, granulation and pale dapples; ink and small-wash decals are then scattered on top. Everything is baked into 256-unit chunks.
layers: Paper base #f5eede modulated by paper tooth (0.95 + 0.075 * noise)
Biome washes from domain-warped fbm fields (forest scale 820, field 640, path 560 units) with signed-distance edges perturbed by flow noise (edge softness 0.45-5.45 units in wet-in-wet zones)
Edge pooling (density up to x1.85 within 2.6 units inside an edge) and 0.75-unit paper gaps between neighbouring washes
Granulation (pigment specks) and pale dapples / backrun rings
Decals: backrun blooms (r 5-16), pigment splatter, path stones, leaf litter, stubble rows, inked grass tufts (3-5 blades, 2.2-5.6 units), tiny flowers, twigs and mushrooms
Y-sorted props (trees, firs, bushes, pumpkins, haystacks, fences, walls, signposts, scarecrows, boulders) as baked sprites
Screen overlay: deckled bare-paper margin (~2.4 % of height) with a faint sienna rim line; an alizarin wash creeps in from the margins when hurt

characters.summary: Characters are assembled from wash shapes (spline outlines with 0.12-0.28 unit jitter) + broken ink contours, baked once per animation pose and 'boil' variant: hero 4 walk poses x 3 boils + 3 idle, enemies 4 poses x 2 boils. The hero is ~18 units wide and ~30 tall (pumpkin head rx 8.5, ry 6.9, body 10 units), feet at the sprite anchor.
rules: Big round head (about half the height), small body, stubby legs: storybook proportions.
Each part = wash (base + 2-3 wet-in-wet blobs + highlight + rim + granulation) followed by a 2-3 piece broken ink outline; draw back limbs first, front arm last.
Faces are carved glowing shapes (warm yellow wash, white core, orange rim, thin ink) or ink dots with heavy tapered brows; readable at 3 px per unit.
The ink contour is thicker on the shadow side (bottom-right), so silhouettes read against the busy ground.
Re-jitter strokes per boil frame (different seeds) and cycle boils at 5-6 fps so the linework lives.
Every actor stands on an indigo glaze shadow ellipse (hero 7.6 x 2.8 units).

effects.name: Paint splatter hit
effects.how: A baked splat sprite (central blot + 9 radiating droplets, ink or orange) flashes for 0.17 s at the hit point; 3 paint-drop particles in the enemy colours fly out with gravity and land as flattened stains on the ground layer.

effects.name: Death dissolve
effects.how: 4 pre-baked dissolve frames per enemy: pixels drip downwards by a per-column random amount and disappear where wash noise < threshold, fading towards paper colour; plus a tinted bloom ring on the ground and 10-22 paint drops.

effects.name: Spawn stain
effects.how: Enemies appear as a soft (4 px blurred) copy over a spreading wash puddle in their colour, the sharp sprite fades in from spawnT 0.35.

effects.name: Seed projectile
effects.how: A small cream seed wash with ink outline, preceded by an 18-unit dry-brush trail: tapered ribbon with an orange gradient and 5 streak gaps cut out (destination-out).

effects.name: Pickup sparkle and level-up bloom
effects.how: Golden 4-point ink-outlined star sprites; level-up adds a gold bloom ring (radial white ring tinted, scaled 10 -> 44 units) and 14 stars.

effects.name: Dash smear
effects.how: Two 22 %/11 % alpha copies of the hero along the dash plus an indigo dry-brush smear sprite of 9 tapered strokes.

effects.name: Damage numbers
effects.how: Caveat 700, 10.5 px (crit 15 px, #9e2a1c on a faint red splat), paper-coloured 2.4-3 px stroke behind, rotated +-0.14 rad, pop-in scale 0.55 -> 1.15.

ui.summary: HUD elements are painted wash strokes inside hand-inked frames on paper: an ochre XP wash bar across the top, a red HP wash bar with ragged right edge, a feathered paper plaque behind the clock with an ink swash ornament, and deckle-edged paper cards for level-up choices.

motion: Hero walk: 4 poses, phase = distance-based anim * 0.8; vertical bob -0.9 * |cos(phase * pi/2)| units; idle bob sin(t * 2.4) * 0.35.
Line boil: hero cycles 3 baked variants at 6 fps, enemies 2 variants at 5 fps (offset by a per-enemy seed).
Small enemy walk 4 poses at anim * 0.7, ghost 0.35, brute 0.45; ghosts float -2.2 + sin(t * 3) * 1.3 units and are drawn at 90 % alpha.
Carved face glow flickers: alpha 0.3 + 0.08 sin(11t) + 0.05 sin(23t), additive.
Gems cycle 3 baked variants at 4 fps; big gems bob 1 unit at 3 rad/s.
Hit splats live 0.17 s, kill rings 1.0-1.4 s, paint drops 0.9-1.7 s with gravity 260 and drag 1.6.
Props in front of the hero (tree crowns) fade to 42 % alpha while the hero is behind them.
do: Mix ground colour per pixel in absorbance space and darken wash edges (pooling).
Draw every coloured shape as wash first, ink second, with the wash offset ~0.45/0.35 units from the ink.
Break contours into 2-3 tapered pieces and make them thicker on the shadow side.
Use wet-in-wet blobs of neighbouring hues (warm light top-left, cool/dark bottom-right) inside each shape.
Keep the ground light and low-chroma; let characters carry the saturated colour.
Bake all sprite frames and boil variants once; per frame only drawImage.
Frame the screen with a deckled bare-paper margin and use storybook serif + handwriting fonts.
dont: Don't use hard flat fills with uniform black strokes (that turns it into cartoon vector art).
Don't use pure black or neutral grey: no #000 ink, no grey shadows.
Don't alpha-blend ground biomes in RGB (muddy grey transitions).
Don't draw continuous perfect outlines or constant line widths.
Don't generate washes per frame with canvas blur filters: it costs milliseconds per sprite.
Don't add glossy specular highlights, neon glows or saturated full-screen effects.
Don't fill the paper margin with game world: the page frame is part of the look.
performance: Expensive at init (1-3 s): 6 noise textures (1024 px wash flow, 256 px paper/grain) by repeated box blur, ~60 character frames, ~25 prop sprites, FX sprites and HUD textures, each wash using canvas blur filters. Ground chunks (256 units, per-pixel shader + decals, up to 2.5 px/unit) are built by a generator that yields every 1-2 rows, so a chunk is spread over frames (5 ms budget). Per frame: chunk blits, one shadow Path2D fill, y-sorted sprite drawImage, a few additive glows and the cached page-margin strips (only the 11 % edge bands are redrawn). No per-frame filters or getImageData.
